pool.text: Francis Light established the Port of Penang as a free port alongside the capital.
The trading port was set up, attracting many diverse cultures to settle in George Town.
The Sultan attempted to recapture the Prince of Wales Island after an agreement breach.
Lieutenant-Governor George Leith secured Province Wellesley across the Penang Strait.
Penang became a separate presidency of British India sharing status with major cities.
The Prince of Wales Island Gazette, the nation's first newspaper, was founded.
Penang fell without struggle to the Imperial Japanese Army after daily aerial attacks.
George Town was the first Malayan settlement liberated by British marines through Operation Jurist.
The Penang Secessionist Committee was formed due to growing economic and ethnic concerns.
George Town's status as a free port was rescinded by the Malaysian federal government.
Chief Minister Lim Chong Eu established the Bayan Lepas Free Industrial Zone.
Time noted that food in the city was exceptionally good and remarkably inexpensive.
Rapid Penang was established as the state's main public transport operator across routes.
UNESCO gazetted nearly 260 ha within downtown George Town as a World Heritage Site.
The state-funded Penang Philharmonic Orchestra was established to elevate classical music standards.
Lithuanian artist Ernest Zacharevic created a series of six local culture wall paintings.
George Town was ranked Malaysia's most attractive destination for commercial property investment.
The George Town Literary Festival achieved the international Literary Festival Award.
An official survey revealed one of the lowest obesity rates in Malaysia.
The Penang Hill Biosphere Reserve was designated a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve for biodiversity.
